fixes.explanation: That's it. Samuel, Israel's prophet, tells them that if they're returning to the LORD with all their hearts, the foreign gods and Ashtoreths have to go (1 Samuel 7:3). Notice he says ALL their hearts, not a nice chunk of them. Half a heart is like an oven on half heat: you wait and wait and still get doughy cookies. Then verse 4 says they put away the Baals and Ashtoreths.

The Egyptians never come up in this passage. Samuel's promise is about the hand of the Philistines. They're the ones who show up marching later in the chapter (1 Samuel 7:7). Right idea of a promise, just a different people.

The Moabites aren't in this story at all. Samuel says the LORD will deliver them from the hand of the Philistines (1 Samuel 7:3). And sure enough, the Philistine rulers are the ones who march up (1 Samuel 7:7).

Not quite, baker. Samuel's offer is to pray to the LORD on their behalf (1 Samuel 7:5). The men of Israel are the ones who charge out of Mizpah, and that comes after the LORD thundered (1 Samuel 7:10-11). Samuel's offer here is prayer.
The ark isn't part of his offer. Verse 2 says it remained at Kiriath-jearim, and Samuel's promise at Mizpah is that he will pray to the LORD on their behalf (1 Samuel 7:5). No hauling required.
They did say something, but "spoken" isn't the word. The people confess, “We have sinned against the LORD.” (1 Samuel 7:6) The word they use is sinned. And they confess it while fasting.

That's the one. Verse 10 says the LORD “…thundered loudly against the Philistines and threw them into such confusion that they fled before Israel.” Samuel was offering up the burnt offering as the Philistines drew near. And the Philistines are the ones who fled.

Right. The Philistines don't hold their ground. The LORD thundered against them and threw them into confusion, and they fled before Israel (1 Samuel 7:10). Then the men of Israel charged out of Mizpah and pursued them (1 Samuel 7:11). Quite a turnaround, baker.
Ebenezer is right. Samuel sets up the stone between Mizpah and Shen and names it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.” (1 Samuel 7:12) Samuel puts those words right with the name.

The Moabites don't appear in this passage. The peace in verse 14 is between the Israelites and the Amorites. The same verse says the cities from Ekron to Gath were restored to Israel. Good guess, but not the one named.
Simple as that. The text says Samuel would return to Ramah “…because his home was there…” (1 Samuel 7:17) After all that traveling, he goes home. I bet that felt good, friend.
The ark isn't the reason given. Verse 2 says it remained at Kiriath-jearim. The reason the text gives for Ramah is that Samuel's home was there (1 Samuel 7:17).
The text gives a different reason. Samuel returned to Ramah “…because his home was there…” (1 Samuel 7:17) His own home is the reason the text names.
No temple here, baker. Samuel builds an altar to the LORD in Ramah (1 Samuel 7:17). A temple doesn't come up anywhere in this passage. An altar is what he builds there.
